subject: Renewal / Reserved Pool Expansion — Velocity Assurance Addendum
messages:
From: Sam Patel <sam@acuityai.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acuityai.com
Date: Mon, 2 Aug 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal + expansion questions — reserved pool tokens/sec expectations

Logan —

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. As we approach our renewal window (ends 2027-08-31) Acuity wants to add a dedicated reserved pool to serve production traffic across our multimodal pipeline. High-level ask: add 24 additional A100-class GPUs in a single reserved pool for US-west to support our expanded LLM footprint.

Two items we want to lock in in the renewal addendum:
- A sustained tokens/sec band for the reserved pool (we're targeting ~220k tokens/sec sustained, 280k tokens/sec burst) with clear fallback behavior.
- An operational SLO that defines acceptable performance degradation and remediation steps (e.g., automatic fallback to compatible model variants, credits on failure to meet contracted throughput).

Attached is a usage profile from July showing peak windows and percentiles — happy to review. Can you send a proposed addendum language and a timeline for reaching PROD? We need procurement and legal to line up PO and signature by Aug 20.

Thanks,
Sam
Sam Patel
Head of Platform Engineering, Acuity AI
(attachment: acuity_usage_profile_jul2027.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet))

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam@acuityai.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Aug 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal + expansion questions — reserved pool tokens/sec expectations

Sam —

Appreciate the usage file — good visibility. We can support the 24 A100-equivalent GPUs in a US-west reserved pool and codify throughput as an addendum. Initial proposal (high level):

1) Capacity: 24x A100-equivalent GPUs reserved for Acuity (single pool).
2) Throughput band: guaranteed steady-state capacity of 220,000 tokens/sec with a documented burst ceiling of 280,000 tokens/sec for scheduling windows up to 10 minutes.
3) SLOs & remedies:
   - Availability SLO: 99.9% of requests served within the contracted throughput band per calendar month.
   - Degradation handling: if throughput falls below 90% of contracted band for >15 continuous minutes, Redwood will trigger autoscaling/burst (if available) and notify Acuity.
   - Credits: pro-rated credits for failure to meet availability SLO >72 cumulative minutes/month (credit schedule to be defined in addendum).
4) Fallback policy: requests that exceed available tokens/sec will be routed to an agreed compatible model variant (lower-cost/latency) unless Acuity elects to throttle. Fallback incidence will be included in monthly ops report.

I'll have a draft addendum from Legal + Sales Ops by EOD Wed (Aug 4). Neha — can you confirm the GPU SKU mapping and whether we should include an explicit KV-cache reservation / prefix caching clause? Marissa — want to loop you for renewal commercial terms.

Next steps:
- Internal draft addendum -> send to Acuity for redline (Wed).
- DocuSign route + PO (target Aug 20).
- Schedule rollout window: two-week lead for capacity provisioning after final signature.

Regards,
Logan Wright
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0147

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal + expansion questions — reserved pool tokens/sec expectations

Sam / Logan —

Quick technical confirmation: 24x A100-equivalent GPUs maps to our "r5-24" reserved profile. Expected steady-state throughput for typical LLM mixes (gpt-like 1.2B-13B mixed calls, ~30 token median responses) is in the 180–260k tokens/sec range depending on batching and KV cache hit rates. To reliably meet 220k sustained we recommend:

- Prefill: enable prefix/KV cache for common prompts (we can reserve up to 8GB of KV cache footprint per pool in this config).
- Batching policy: continuous batching with a 20ms max hold time to balance latency and throughput.
- Quantization: we suggest q4f16 for larger models to reduce memory pressure and improve tokens/sec.
- Autoscale & burst: we can provide 1.25x burst capacity (subject to pool headroom) but include a documented cooldown to avoid oscillation.

I've attached a draft addendum with explicit SLO wording for throughput, remediation steps, and a sample credit schedule. Please review and send any redlines.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks — the technical language looks good. A couple of clarifications from procurement/legal:

- Need an explicit definition of "sustained" (we propose sustained = 10-minute rolling average).

Assuming those are acceptable we'll route to our legal for a quick redline and request DocuSign. Can you also send final pricing for the 24x pool and a PO template?

Sam
